annotations.text:
A · VERDICT FIRST

The read is the page. One conclusion per company at 40px, everything else demoted to evidence beneath it.

Fixes: the thing you actually want to know stops competing with ten equal-weight panels.

Costs: a graded, caveated model rendered as a big confident word. Risks overclaiming — the opposite of this codebase's instincts.

B · TERMINAL

No cards. Rules, columns, monospace, a command bar. Every signal for both names on one screen with no scrolling.

Fixes: density and cross-signal comparison — you read across the matrix in one pass.

Costs: unwelcoming to anyone who isn't in it daily, and hostile to the caveats this model depends on.

C · LAYERED WORKSPACE

A rail of signal groups, one focused work area, a permanent trust inspector on the right.

Fixes: gives provenance a fixed home — grade, data days, repaired days, caveats always visible.

Costs: you drill instead of scan, and it hides the cross-signal comparison B is best at.

Direction A carried onto Overview — same hierarchy move: one plain-language sentence of state-of-play on top, the numbers demoted beneath it. Included so you can judge the system, not just one screen.

CONTROL CHARTS, REAL DATA

Every line is computed from fct_channel_daily and fct_adjusted_price_daily — SVG coordinates generated in SQL, not sketched. MA30 back-solves to 38,948,134 views/day, matching a figure verified independently earlier.

Limits are ±1σ and ±2σ around the 110-day mean. The five lines sit at exactly even 47–48px spacing, which is itself the check that the scale is linear.

WHY THE WINDOWS ARE FACETED

Four moving averages of one measure is a sequential relationship, so the instinct is one hue in four steps. The palette validator rejected every such ramp: adjacent steps land at ΔE 8–13, below the 15 floor where full-colour vision can still separate them.

Each window gets its own panel on a shared scale instead. Level differences read directly, and it survives any colour vision.

THE NULL RESULT IS THE RESULT

Three metrics × two companies × fifteen lags = 90 tests. Only 3 clear the nominal 5% line — chance alone predicts 4.5. None survive FDR correction.

Correlations use daily LOG RETURNS, not price levels: two trending series correlate with almost anything, and that artefact is the most common way this analysis is got wrong. Dual-axis was never an option for the same reason.
